title: Voice Agents Can Just Do Things — Charlie Guo, OpenAI
talk_summary: Charlie Guo argues voice agents don't have to reply with speech, outlining three modes (speech-to-speech, speech-to-action, event-to-speech) and urging developers to expose existing app verbs/endpoints as tools. The only concrete engineering claims are that native-audio realtime models cut latency versus chained transcribe→LLM→TTS pipelines, and that 'preamble' prompts let a model announce work while it calls tools.

takeaways.technique: Preamble/status announcements before long tool work
takeaways.what_they_do: Prompt the agent to emit a short heads-up message before it starts thinking or calling tools, so the user knows work is in progress rather than seeing silence.
takeaways.evidence_quote: preamles are a way that you can prompt the model to uh give the user a heads up if it's going to be thinking or if it's going to be calling tools

takeaways.technique: Expose existing app verbs as agent tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat API endpoints and UI actions as nouns/verbs that can be wrapped as tools for a model, rather than building new agent-specific interfaces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you already expose so much of it as like action as nouns and verbs ... Each of those things can like pretty relatively easily be converted into a tool

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a model trained on native audio tokens instead of transcribe→LLM→synthesize chains, because chaining adds latency and loses signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the first two uh voice modes in chat GBT were built with this chained approach ... had you know significantly higher latency than using uh the native approach
